window.note: WATCHME armed at cairn/devices/tester/probes/the_collapse_holds_in_live_traffic.py — the berth the ticket's spec names, a frozen Probe carrying both carry and enough. IT WATCHES WHAT NO FIXTURE CAN SEE: whether the corpus AGREES to live one-record. This store has lost that bet before — the door was sealed 2026-08-05 with three physics layers and its proofs went green, and within two days two voyages wrote six trails around it. Trigger: 20+ post-collapse records AND at least one file holding more than one. Enough: the same floor with zero offenders — THE FLOOR SITS ON BOTH CLAUSES, because without it on the clear side an empty post-collapse corpus retires the watch on its first pulse (the asymmetry that let does_optional_mean_never_carried clear at n=1 against a corpus of one ticket, itself). Measured now: post_collapse=5 against a floor of 20 — neither fires nor clears, the resting state a just-armed watch belongs in, and a planted two-record file raised multi_count to 1 without firing, the floor holding under a real violation rather than in argument. AND ITS SIBLING WAS RETIRED IN THE SAME ACT: the_door_is_the_only_path_in_practice counted entries carrying no trail_link, and the chain retired with the append-only-ness it protected, so that key is now written by nothing — left standing it would have read a corpus-wide zero forever and fired on a finding false by construction. The first fix (keep it, re-instrument it onto this survey) was MEASURED WRONG during the build: two probes computing one number and clearing on one condition is the REPEATS class probescan already counts as a defect. Retiring a probe berthed with the tester is a write the charter's gated_by admits (Law 6); the reason rides the surviving probe's docstring rather than being inferable from an absent file. probescan reports 0 references to it and test_watchme_spec.py reads 13/14 before and after — the same pre-existing red, naming six other tickets, not this one. THE BUILD GATE REFUSED THIS CROSSING ONCE, correctly: survey holding 9 charted the retired probe's address hours before the build removed it, and the sieve cannot tell a deliberate retirement from the drift it was taught by. The disposition is the corpus's own mechanism, not a paragraph — a forwarding order on this ticket naming the successor that carries the question, both ends checked in the world, exactly as watchme-emits-a-probe disposed of the renames its own decompose ordered. The berth was not touched.

window.note: A VALIDATION IS ONE CURRENT RECORD, NOT A TRAIL — Akien's ruling of 2026-08-16 built and proved. persist_validation REPLACES the standing record, and a DIFFERING incoming verdict raises a trouble through TroubleDevice BEFORE the replace lands: announce-then-write is the whole of what makes the collapse legal under Law 7, because announcing after would let a crash lose the change AND the record it replaced, while announcing first can at worst raise a false alarm. The one-time collapse printed 'collapsed 54 files; dropped 193 superseded records into git'; the corpus now reads 91 files, 91 records, max 1 per file, and only 2 of the 54 held a verdict change at all — the trail was 52-of-54 repetition, which is what the ruling's 'it tends to create noise' names. THE CHAIN RETIRED WITH WHAT IT PROTECTED: _link_for was an importable pure function, so anyone could mint a link that verified — measured, with a forger's trail standing green — and the unforgeability was never bought. What the chain bought was deletion-detection, i.e. the append-only-ness this ticket spends, so it retired with it. Four honest layers remain (the 0444 mode bit, the build-time second-writer scan, source_fingerprint, git), and the new instrument is strictly harder to fake than the link it replaced: producing a two-record file REQUIRES doing the exact thing being watched for. Verdict artifact verdict-20260816T142450-26f633a38b9a.json answers all 7 validate criteria pass, with 9 of 10 hypotheses confirmed and 1 KILLED. THE CORRECTIONS THIS CROSSING CARRIES, because a green that hides them teaches nothing. (1) TOOTH COUNT: the PROVEME note two crossings back says '13/13 teeth' and the file measures 14 — a hand's miscount, and the proof's own roster floor had been written 13 from the same miscount, leaving room for exactly the one disappearance a floor exists to catch. History is append-only so that note stands; the floor is raised to 14, the reason is recorded in-file, and this record is the correction. (2) A SIBLING PROBE RETIRED: the_door_is_the_only_path_in_practice counted entries carrying no trail_link, a key now written by nothing; the first fix — keep it and re-instrument it — was measured wrong in-build (two probes, one number, one clearing condition: probescan's own REPEATS class), so it is gone and its question is carried by the armed probe, with the reason in that probe's docstring and a forwarding order on the ticket naming the successor, both ends checked in the world. (3) ONE UNEXPLAINED TRANSIENT: the first corpus sweep printed 111 proofs / 108 green / 3 red and the third red's identity was not captured because only the tail was kept; three later sweeps print 109/2, the two pre-existing reds (test_route.py, test_watchme_spec.py, both already standing troubles). Recorded rather than rounded off — the method fix is to tee the whole sweep. (4) THE FIRST DRAFT OF THE ANNOUNCEMENT GUARD keyed on class-space and passed its own proofs while being wrong: quorum.seal addresses CairnCommons concept-pieces, so it would have silenced every human-proved review flip. The guard predicate is the TEMP ROOT, and the charter's falsifier now names that mistake as clause (8). LIVE FIRE: a green-then-red pair sealed at a real class-space address raised validation-verdict-changed-live-fire-artifact in the real trouble store, and `bin/cmd/slate` rendered it at the top of the session banner — the human surface the criterion demanded. Cleared through TroubleDevice.clear afterwards; the scratch artifact was never committed.
